To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified two novel factors involved in the regulation of dimorphism and pathogenesis in Z. tritocii, the causal agent of Septoria tritici blotch, one of the most devastating diseases of wheat worldwide.
we identified genes encoding factors involved in the dimorphic switch of Zymosepetoria tritici, which are essential for the virulence of this fungus.

the forward genetics approach applied in this thesis allowed the identification of novel genes involved in dimorphism of Zymosepetoria tritici and furthermore revealed their function in the pathogenicity of the fungus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes involved in dimorphism in Z. triticia and the elucidation of their biological role within pathogenicity.
the identification of factors involved in morphogenetic transition of the wheat pathogenic fungi Z. triticia.
the elucidation of molecular basis of morphogenetic transition of Z. tritiici, a key factor for virulence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the identified genes are essential for pathogenic lifestyle of Z. tritic, since they are crucial for dimorphic switch and virulence.
both identified genes are essential for Z. triticia to successfully infect its host and to complete the infection cycle, thus representing novel targets for future breeding strategies.
both genes identified are involved in morphogenetic switching and pathogenicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the forward genetics approach applied is a suitable method to identify genes involved in morphological transition and pathogenicity.

the forward genetic approach applied is a suitable tool for identification of genes involved in morphological transition of Z. tritic and that the genes identified are involved in pathogenicity of the pathogenic fungus.
this study represents the first report of a forward genetics approach to identify genes involved in the morphogenetic transition in a filamentous plant pathogenic fungus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a plate-based screening approach is a powerful tool to investigate the molecular background of fungal dimorphism.
the described screening approach is a suitable method for the identification of novel factors involved in dimorphic transition in Z. triticio.

a forward genetics approach in combination with an established ATMT system is a powerful tool to study the molecular basis of complex biological processes like morphological transition and to investigate their impact in pathogenesis.
